candidates.rationale: No deterministic upsize signal and downsize safety criteria are not all satisfied.
Queueing crosses the increase thresholds, but the configuration epoch, query sample or queued-query count is too new/small to act on; no change is recommended.
The current configuration is not ready yet (too few settled billed days) to measure its idle gaps; auto-stop is re-evaluated once it is.
Serverless is evaluated as a separate migration experiment with a pre-canary DBU/AWS counterfactual and deterministic compatibility gate.

assumptions: Current configuration epoch is the decision baseline.
Forward DBU cost uses the deterministic current-epoch run-rate model.
AWS forward cost is modeled from observed current-epoch resource time and the configured regional price registry when available.
DBU cost is priced at the account's list price; negotiated discounts lower real savings in proportion.
AWS cost is priced at on-demand EC2 rates; Spot, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are not modeled.

reevaluation.method: Later of the active gates: the next settled day, 00:00Z of the analysis date + 1 day (readiness: 2 settled billed days in the current epoch) and 00:00Z of epoch start date + 7 days (cost-history floor). Earliest only: billing ingestion lag, days without billing and query-sample gates can delay it.
